new_packages.label: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְחֵלֶק בֵּאלֹהִים
new_packages.label_en: Eretz Yisrael and a Portion in God
new_packages.reason: Three bechina-linked nodes from the source text (zero dataset edges for reference 104). The Gemara (Ketubot 110b) establishes that dwelling in Eretz Yisrael IS having God — a shared-nature identity, not cause and effect. כְּשֵׁרִים (the innocent/worthy) are those who embody this connection through their desire for the Land.

new_packages.label: חוּץ לָאָרֶץ וְאֵין לוֹ אֱלוֹהַּ
new_packages.reason: The evil mirror of Package 1. Exile from the Land, having no God, and idol worship are three faces of the same essential spiritual disconnection. The Gemara's keillu declaration makes exile and having no God a bechina identity; idol worship is the concrete embodiment of that same state.

observations: Torah #104 has zero bechina edges in torahData.js. Both packages are built entirely from gap analysis of the source text. The teaching's entire bechina structure rests on the Talmudic identity declaration in Ketubot 110b ('כָּל הַדָּר בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ כְּאִלּוּ אֵין לוֹ אֱלוֹהַּ') and its positive inverse (dwelling in the Land = having God). Both packages exceed the 3-node threshold (Package 1: 3 nodes, Package 2: 3 nodes) and form fully independent domains — a good/evil mirror pair that is the complete structure of the Torah. The concept חוֹשֵׁד בִּכְשֵׁרִים (suspecting the innocent, from Shabbat 97) was evaluated as an eitza node (the mechanism of Moshe's punishment), not a bechina node, and was excluded from both packages.
